title: Centre declares Shahzad Bhatti Network a terrorist group under UAPA
author: Vijaita Singh
content_html:
The Union government on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) designated the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN) a terrorist group under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).

The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said in a notification that through its terrorist activities, the outfit led by Pakistani gangster Shahzad Bhatti poses a “serious threat to the democratic system, communal harmony, and internal security of the country”.

On Independence Day, over 200 people were arrested in a country-wide anti-terror operation that was linked to the SBN.

Bhatti, who speaks Punjabi and has a significant social media presence with regular posts on Instagram and Facebook, has been operating out of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), according to officials. Over the last one and a half years, he is said to have “graduated” from organised crime to “terror-related activities”.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said in a post on X, “Pursuing PM Shri @narendramodi [Narendra Modi] Ji’s vision of zero tolerance against terror, the MHA declares the Shahzad Bhatti Network as a terrorist organisation under the UAPA.” The SBN is the 46th group to be designated a “terrorist organisation” under the UAPA.

From smuggling to radicalisation

Without mentioning the specific cases against the network, the MHA notification listed nine categories of crimes registered against the group under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Information Technology Act, the Explosives Substances Act, the UAPA, the Official Secrets Act, the Immigration and Foreigners Act, and the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act.

The MHA described the SBN as an organisation that aimed to involve gullible youth and local criminals in the smuggling of arms, explosives, and narcotics from across the border. Through terrorist activities, the group also poses a serious threat to the democratic system, communal harmony, and internal security of the country, the Ministry said. It added that “several criminal cases” have been duly registered against those linked to the SBN, across multiple jurisdictions, for their involvement in unlawful and terrorist activities.

It further said that SBN is involved in radicalising vulnerable youth by offering various allurements, motivating them towards anti-national activities, and mobilising resources for anti-national acts in collusion with other banned organisations and designated entities.

“SBN is promoting terrorism through violent activities that disrupt public order, and by using various digital communication platforms to disseminate provocative messages, posing a serious challenge to the integrity of the nation... The Central Government believes that ‘Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN)’ is involved in terrorism and has participated in various acts of terrorism in India,” the notification said.

title: Don’t trust verbal promises of Centre: Omar Abdullah tells Ladakh leaders
author: Peerzada Ashiq
content_html:
J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) advised Ladakh leaders “not to trust verbal promises of the Centre.”

“I can advise them (Ladakh leaders) as a friend and elder brother: Do not trust the verbal promises of the Centre. We have suffered it on the demand of Statehood. We were promised Statehood immediately after the assembly elections. Around two years have already passed,” Mr. Abdullah said.

The J&K Chief Minister made a hand-folded appeal to agitating Ladakh leaders “to seek a signed and a written affidavit” from the Centre. “Till Ladakh does not have anything in writing, they will not achieve anything,” Mr. Abdullah said.

His statement came following the September 9 talks between Ladakh representatives, including members of socio-religious organisations of Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), and the Centre.

In spite of the Centre terming the talks “successful”, both the LAB and KDA are sceptical and have decided to step up protests on the first anniversary of the death of four civilians on September 24 last year. The LAB and KDA leaders are demanding a draft paper on the promises made by the Centre to grant special status under special provisions under Article 371.

LAB co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook and KDA co-chairman Asgar Ali Karbalai on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) hinted at holding “peaceful” protests ahead of the first anniversary of the September 24 violence, which left four dead and around 90 injured last year.

title: India rejects Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission ‘which is without any legal basis’
author: PTI
content_html:
India on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) rejected the "so-called" boundary joint commission set up by Pakistan and China, saying that the body has no legal basis to decide on arrangements related to Indian territory under illegal occupation.

New Delhi's reaction came following the first meeting of the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission in Islamabad.

Our response to media queries on the so-called Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission ⬇️

🔗 https://t.co/i3x1x8eluCpic.twitter.com/Nt6QfhHqjA

— Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) September 16, 2026

India has been consistently maintaining that Pakistan's handing over of certain territories such as Shaksgam Valley to China in 1963 was illegal and unacceptable.

New Delhi has also opposed the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor as part of it passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). "Our position on this matter is clear and consistent. There is no boundary between Pakistan and China. We reject the so-called Joint Commission, which is without any legal basis," External Affairs Ministry spokesman Randhir Jaiswal said on the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission.

The entire Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh "have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India", he said.

"We have never recognised the so-called 'China-Pakistan Boundary Agreement' of 1963 and have consistently maintained that it is illegal and invalid," Mr. Jaiswal said.

The spokesperson added: "We resolutely oppose and reject any attempts to alter the status of these occupied territories or legitimise illegal occupation, impinging on India's sovereignty and territorial integrity." "Any so-called boundary cooperation between China and Pakistan concerning Indian territories would be completely unacceptable and would have no bearing whatsoever on India's sovereignty over these territories," he said.

"Instead of engaging in such theatrics, we call on Pakistan to immediately vacate areas under its illegal and forcible occupation," Mr. Jaiswal said.

title: Twenty seven people, including senior Congress leaders Vidya Charan Shukla, Nand Kumar Patel, and Mahendra Karma, were killed in the attack on May 25, 2013
author: Shubhomoy Sikdar
content_html:
A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Chhattisgarh’s Jagdalpur has awarded death sentences to all 10 convicts in the 2013 Jhiram Valley Maoist attack. Twenty seven people, including senior Congress leaders Vidya Charan Shukla, Nand Kumar Patel, and Mahendra Karma, were killed in the attack on May 25, 2013.

“Today, the NIA Special Court, Jagdalpur, awarded the death penalty to all 10 convicted accused persons, having found them guilty under sections 147, 148, 149, 121, 121(A), 122, 341, 302, 307, 396, 397, 427 and 120(B) of the IPC [Indian Penal Code, 1860], sections 25 and 27 of the Arms Act [, 1959], sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Explosive Substances Act, and sections 16, 18, 20, 38, 39 and 40 of the UA (P) Act [Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967], in NIA case RC-06/2013/NIA/DLI (Jheeram Ghati Attack),” the NIA said in a release issued on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).

Guilty verdict

Earlier on September 5, the NIA court convicted 10 persons — Pramila Modiyam, Chaitu Lekam alias Munna, Sumitra alias Sumitra Punem Modiyam, Mukka Mandvi, Kosa Kavasi alias Kosaram, Aayata Markam, Madkami Deva, Joga Madkami, Banjami Snna alias Chamru alias Denga, and Mahadev Nag — for the killings.

During the trial, the agency informed the court that members of the banned Communist Party of India (Maoist) attacked a convoy of about 20 vehicles carrying Congress leaders. The attackers triggered a landmine blast that blocked the route of the vehicles participating in the Parivartan Yatra. This was followed by indiscriminate firing and grenade lobbing, resulting in 24 deaths on the spot and injuries to over 35 persons.

Senior Congress leaders Nand Kumar Patel, Mahendra Karma, Uday Mudaliyar, Dinesh Patel, and 10 police personnel were among those killed on the spot. Later, three victims, including former Union Minister V.C. Shukla, succumbed to injuries.

The attackers stole nine AK-47 rifles, seven INSAS rifles, two SLRs, four 9mm pistols and magazines before fleeing.

The NIA had filed charges against 39 people, including two top Maoist leaders, Thippiri Tirupathi alias Devuji and Barse Deva, who have surrendered recently. Although they were chargesheeted, they were listed as wanted while the trial was ongoing. The initial trial against the 10 chargesheeted persons concluded after recording evidence from 101 prosecution witnesses. One accused died in judicial custody during the trial.

“NIA’s investigation established that armed cadres of the banned terrorist organisation CPI (Maoist), in connivance with local committees and divisions, were part of a criminal conspiracy to attack and kill senior Congress leaders and security personnel in the convoy of the Parivartan Yatra, in pursuance of their Tactical Counter Offensive Campaign (TCOC),” an NIA official said.

Congress protest

Opposition Congress leaders, who had earlier expressed dissatisfaction over the guilty verdict, reiterated their stance on Wednesday (September 16, 2026). They have demanded that senior Maoist leaders involved in the conspiracy behind the Jheeram attack be booked and that the political conspiracy angle be probed.

“Those who hatched the conspiracy and those who executed the massacre are still roaming free. At whose behest, one wonders, the NIA had already dropped the names of top Naxalite leaders; they were not even charged. Neither the NIA nor the commission of inquiry investigated the conspiracy. BJP leaders consistently created hurdles and prevented the investigation from taking place. There is no question of the court’s verdict altering our perspective. We still maintain that justice remains incomplete because the investigation itself was incomplete,” former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel posted on X.

Chief Minister’s reaction

Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai hailed the verdict as a victory for justice and credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for eradicating Naxalism from the country.

“The death penalty handed down by the Jagdalpur NIA court to the 10 Maoists found guilty in the case is a victory for justice. The manner in which the NIA conducted this investigation should also be commended. Today, under the iron resolve and strong leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, we have liberated the State from the clutches of armed Maoism. Bastar, which suffered Maoist violence for decades, is now moving towards a new era of peace, trust, and development,” Mr. Sai said.

The Chief Minister further said that the occasion was also a time for introspection, especially for those who play “politics on the corpse of tribal communities and those who provide intellectual and ideological support to terrorism”.

Meanwhile, human rights organisation People’s Union for Civil Liberties expressed concern over the death sentence.

“The imposition of capital punishment in this case also raises grave concerns of unequal access to justice, individual culpability, and the disproportionate impact of the harshest punishments upon the poorest and most marginalised sections of society,” a PUCL statement read.

title: Falsely quoting judges in barred online court clips is criminal conduct, says Supreme Court
author: Krishnadas Rajagopal
content_html:
The Supreme Court clarified on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) that while unauthorised distribution of live-streamed proceedings constitutes contempt, circulating clips featuring false insertions or misattributed judicial remarks graduates the violation into criminal conduct.

A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant was referring to the online representation of oral remarks made during court proceedings.

The court said falsely imputing statements as part of oral submissions made by lawyers in court was also wrong.

The Bench was hearing a petition filed by a lawyer who complained that a video of his appearance in court was circulated online by portals and social media sites in violation of specific Supreme Court orders on July 24 and July 31, which had barred the online use of raw or edited audio and video clippings of judicial hearings.

The lawyer said the circulation of the video had caused him reputational harm while practising his profession.

On July 24, the court had passed an interim direction prohibiting extraction, dissemination, monetisation, posting, re-posting, uploading, transmitting, modification, storing, or hosting of the audio-video recording(s) of judicial proceedings on social media or any other digital platforms without prior permission of the Secretary General of the Supreme Court or the Registrars General of the jurisdictional High Courts.

A week later, on July 31, the apex court issued a clarification stating that its July 24 order did not constitute a blanket prohibition on court coverage by recognised media outlets, provided audio or video clips of the proceedings were not utilised.

‘Be brave’: CJI to lawyer

The petitioner-lawyer said he was only making an appearance in his professional capacity in a bail matter.

The Chief Justice reminded him that he had appeared in open court. “Why do you want to hide? You should be brave enough,” the CJI told the legal practitioner.

Questioning the basis of the lawyer’s grievance, the CJI said his allegation did not include that the video circulated online was fabricated or AI was used to cause him harm.

The court said mere online utilisation of livestreamed videos, possibly for commercial exploitation, attracts contempt. However, far more serious would be the adding words never spoken or falsely attributing remarks to the Bench or the lawyers.

“Assuming a channel is putting out videos [of court proceedings], they might be committing contempt. But if they are adding something that you have not spoken, or they attribute something to the Bench that we had never said… That would be a more offending situation because then they are indulging in a criminal activity. That will require a serious view,” Chief Justice Kant addressed the counsel on the petitioner side.

Justice Joymalya Bagchi, on the Bench along with Justice V. Mohana, advised the petitioner to move the authorities under the Information Technology (IT) Act for an order to service providers to ‘take down’ the videos.

“First take the necessary steps for takedown orders under the IT Act. If the takedown orders are not complied with, then you come to us. Exhaust your statutory remedies first,” Justice Bagchi said.

The petitioner withdrew his petition to approach authorities under the relevant law.

title: Trump lauds India's crackdown on poppy farming; lists 23 major drug transit nations
author: PTI
content_html:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) welcomed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to curb illicit poppy cultivation even as he identified India, China and Pakistan among 23 major drug transit and illicit drug producing countries and urged their respective leaders to address the issue.

In a Presidential Determination to the U.S. Congress, Mr. Trump said he looks forward to continued cooperation through the United States-India Drug Policy Framework.

“I welcome Prime Minister Modi and the Government of India’s efforts to address illicit opium poppy cultivation and bolster supply chain integrity," he said in the official directive that was made public on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).

Mr. Trump also made it clear that appearing on the list of major drug transit and illicit drug producing countries was not necessarily a reflection of the respective government’s current counterdrug efforts, or coordination with the U.S.

The Presidential Determination said countries are placed on the list, as required by U.S. law, due to a combination of geographic, commercial, and economic factors that allow drugs or precursor chemicals to transit or be produced, even if a government has engaged in robust and diligent narcotics control and law enforcement measures.

The other major drug transit or major illicit drug producing countries identified are Afghanistan, The Bahamas, Belize, Bolivia, Burma, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Laos, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

Mr. Trump also highlighted the "historic progress" made by his administration in tackling drug trafficking and narcoterrorist organisations. He pointed to tighter border security, lower drug seizures and a decline in overdose deaths as evidence of the progress.

Mr. Trump claimed drug seizures along the U.S. southern border had dropped by more than half after what he called four years of "open border chaos". He also said drug overdose deaths had "plunged" and claimed that the administration had saved tens of thousands of American lives.

“After four years of open border chaos, seizures of fentanyl and other drugs being smuggled into the United States have been reduced by more than half, and drug overdose deaths have plunged,” Mr. Trump said.

He urged China to take stronger action to stem the flow of precursor chemicals used to produce fentanyl, methamphetamine and other synthetic drugs. “The PRC continues to be the world’s largest producer of many of the precursor chemicals used to illicitly produce fentanyl, methamphetamine, and other deadly synthetic drugs,” Mr. Trump said, referring to China by its official designation, the People's Republic of China.

title: Three rescued orangutans in Odisha suffering from anaemia: Officials
author: PTI
content_html:
Three of the five baby orangutans rescued in Odisha are suffering from anaemia, officials said on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).

A comprehensive health check-up of the primates, including X-rays and blood tests, was carried out after one of the juvenile orangutans developed fever, they said.

According to a health bulletin issued by the Nandankanan Zoological Park, where the orangutans have been quarantined, in-house haematology analysis found severe anaemia in one of the primates and mild anaemia in two others.

"Supportive supplementation for the said orangutan babies, as advised by the Technical Committee, has already been started," it said.

"X-rays of the chest, abdomen and skull were taken, while blood, serum and nasopharyngeal swab samples were collected from all five animals. Laboratory tests are underway," it added.

Nandankanan Zoological Park Director Sanath Kumar N. said the overall health condition of the orangutans appeared to be stable.

Four of the five animals recorded a body temperature of 98.4 degrees Fahrenheit, while a male orangutan recorded 99 degrees Fahrenheit, an official said.

"This particular male orangutan has shown a slightly higher temperature than the others since its arrival at Nandankanan Zoological Park on the night of September 8," he said.

The blood samples are also being tested for parameters such as haemoglobin and white blood cell count, while stool and urine samples are being examined, he said.

The samples will also be used for DNA testing to establish the origin of the rescued animals, which could aid the ongoing investigation into suspected wildlife smuggling, he added.

A laboratory capable of conducting the DNA test is being identified, the official said, adding that the facility would need to have standard DNA profiles of orangutans for comparison. "Such laboratories are not very common," he said.

Aditya Acharya, head of the Centre for Wildlife Health (CWH) at Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology, said the well-being of the animals was the priority. "Regarding DNA tests, zoo authorities will take the call on where and when to send the samples," he said.

The five orangutans were rescued from a forest in Balasore district on September 8.

According to a dietary chart prepared by experts, the orangutan babies are being fed milk every two hours, besides apple and banana fluids and boiled potatoes at regular intervals.

No major breakthrough in probe so far

The Odisha Police's Special Task Force (STF) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), which are jointly investigating the suspected international wildlife smuggling that led to the animals being brought to the State, have made no major breakthrough in the probe so far, officials said.

Bhograi MLA Goutam Buddha Das of the BJD criticised the State government over the pace of the investigation and urged Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi to hand over the case to a central agency such as the CBI or NIA. "Since there is an element of international smuggling involved in the case, a high-level and professional probe is most essential," Das said.

BJP spokesperson Anil Biswal, however, said the Odisha Police STF was capable of resolving the case with the assistance of the WCCB. "The BJD MLA is politicising the matter out of nothing," Biswal said.

Orangutans are not native to India and are primarily found in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra, officials said.

title: Rajasthan achieves plantation target ahead of schedule
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Rajasthan has achieved the target of planting 10 crore saplings, originally set for 2026-27 under the ‘Hariyalo Rajasthan’ campaign, ahead of schedule. The mission, launched in August 2024, aims at making the desert State greener and enhance its environmental health and prosperity.

Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) that the initiatives such as ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign had fostered widespread public awareness by linking environment conservation with an emotional bond.

“This sentiment has evolved into a massive public movement through the ‘Hariyalo Rajasthan’ campaign. It is a significant step towards ensuring environment conservation through public participation,” Mr. Sharma said.

Mr. Sharma said the planting of 10 crore saplings stood as a powerful symbol of Rajasthan’s collective commitment to nature. The people participating in the drive would take care of every planted sapling, he said.

The State is also implementing the “one district one species” programme to promote native plant species and protect biodiversity, while special attention has been paid to desert districts such as Barmer and Jaisalmer to combat desertification.

Under the Aravali Green Development Project, ₹250 crore has been invested in 19 districts for soil development and plantation efforts.

title: Rajasthan urban local body elections: Candidates for mayors, chairpersons file nominations
author: PTI
content_html:
The process for the election of mayors and chairpersons in Rajasthan's 305 urban local bodies began on Wednesday with candidates from the BJP, Congress and other parties, besides Independents, filing nominations.

According to a list containing 989 nominations, multiple nominations have been filed in several urban bodies, including cases where the same candidate figures more than once.

The elections are being held for heads of municipal corporations, municipal councils and municipalities following the election of councillors earlier this month.

The State Election Commission had issued a public notice for election of mayors and chairpersons in 305 of the 309 urban local bodies on Tuesday.

The election process has, however, been deferred in four urban bodies — Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota municipal corporations and Suket municipality in Kota district — where re-polling was held at 10 polling stations on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) after results in some wards could not be declared due to EVM-related technical problems.

Counting of the re-poll will be held on Thursday (September 17, 2026). The process for electing the mayors/chairperson and their deputies in these four urban bodies will be taken up later under a revised schedule to be issued by the State Election Commission.

For the 305 urban local bodies, election of mayors and chairpersons is scheduled for September 21, while deputy mayors, deputy chairpersons and vice-presidents will be elected on September 22.
